scope: one P1 walking style study; other four motions and P2 unchanged
prompts:
Use case: precise-object-edit / style-transfer.
IMAGE 1 is the P1 walking dog to EDIT. IMAGE 2 is ONLY a reference for a child's spontaneous crayon mark-making, natural drawing imperfection and INCOMPLETE COLOR COVERAGE. It is NOT a reference for palette, dog anatomy, upright tail, standing pose or markings.
Make one revised P1 illustration keeping image 1's walking pose, same connected four limbs, underlying proportions, short floppy ears, soft muzzle/beard shape, small ROUND dark dot eyes, white central forehead-to-muzzle area, white bib/lower paws, gray outer face/ears/back/flank, and LOW trailing long-haired tail. Same square canvas and near-foot baseline, whole dog in frame. Do not change the dog into the differently shaped animal in image 2. Do not copy its blue/red/green/orange contours.
KEY CHANGE: this should look like an actual child drew it with a few ordinary crayons, with a LOT of paper left uncolored, matching image 2's sparseness. Current P1 is too densely shaded with elaborate fur. REMOVE almost all of those many interior fur strokes and all dense filling. Within the existing GRAY marking regions, use only a FEW irregular loosely spaced light gray crayon strokes; leave MOST of each gray region's interior as untouched paper. Some strokes stop early or stray just barely beyond their outline. Keep broad blank gaps and uneven pressure rather than evenly distributed distressed texture. White fur regions should simply be untouched paper, no beige fill, no hair shading. The gray/white marking layout remains readable from sparse gray hints; do not invent different patches or erase the individual identity.
NATURAL ASYMMETRY: the hand-drawn contour gently wobbles, has a few small open gaps, occasional lightly retraced segments and slightly unequal pressure. Ear contours and toe marks need not be perfectly paired; give them small uneven hand-drawn imperfections while preserving their actual matching anatomical scale and joints. Both eyes remain small round dots without highlights, with subtly imperfect crayon edges. Do NOT introduce different-length legs, a twisted skeleton, large distorted ears, gross asymmetry, strange necks, or a grotesque caricature. Incompleteness belongs to the DRAWN LINE and AMOUNT OF FILL, not to injured or distorted anatomy.
Use the EXISTING P1 gray/white/charcoal palette and a plain warm cream paper background. The user means how fully an area is colored, NOT a request to change hue. No rainbow outlines, no new saturated colors, glossy eyes, excessive cute embellishments, realistic fur, gradients, shadows, vector polish, uniformly noisy full-region fill, text, props, UI or annotations. A simple confident naive child's drawing with empty space, not an accomplished detailed pet portrait with a crayon filter.

Edit image 1 one further step toward image 2's actual naive CHILD DRAWING LINE QUALITY. Image 1 already has suitably incomplete gray filling; keep the SAME gray and paper-white color arrangement, approximate fill amount, same walking pose, small ROUND dot eyes and LOW feathered tail.
The remaining issue is that image 1's outline and gray scribbles still look like an accomplished illustrator rendering realistic fur with a crayon filter. Replace that with the economy of image 2: thin uneven ordinary crayon lines, a few gently wobbly contours, small accidental gaps and occasional retracing, VERY FEW hair tips. Outline the head, body and paws using simple continuous-ish childlike arcs, NOT a ring of tiny fur hatch strokes. Gray fill should be a handful of rough loose back-and-forth strokes with abundant blank paper, NOT repeated fine parallel fur strands or uniform noise. Retain recognizable gray ears/outer face/back/flank and blank white blaze/muzzle/bib/paws. Blank gaps inside a gray region are unfinished coloring, not new stripe markings. Keep a few long strokes to indicate tail feathering without detailed hairs.
Subtle drawing asymmetry: a slightly imperfect ear outline or different toe ticks, not exact mirrored linework. Keep the same underlying ear sizes, limb lengths, head/body proportions and connected joints. No anatomical distortion, grotesque exaggeration, huge eyes, long neck or additional paws. The face should be simple dot eyes, dark nose and a small uncomplicated mouth with tongue; no beige fur-shading, highlights, gradients or cute decorations.
IMPORTANT: image 2 supplies only irregular linework and incomplete filling. Do not import its rainbow colors, erect tail or different dog anatomy. Preserve P1's gray/white/charcoal palette, 1254 square composition and grounded pose. No labels, UI, props or background scene. This must visibly look LESS finished and LESS professionally shaded while remaining a friendly recognizable drawing of the SAME individual.
user_direction: natural childlike drawing asymmetry and incomplete filling; filling means area coverage, not hue
separation: rendering imperfection, not observed individual anatomical asymmetry or new white patches
